title: SlipX sensor configuration
description:
sensors.yaml: sensor instances, their schedules, transport and model parameters.

Consumed since 0.5.0 by the sensor rig (ADR-0047): the loader maps each entry onto the matching sensor model's parameter struct and refuses, naming the sensor and the field, anything it cannot fill (ADR-0048). Each entry may carry a block named after its type holding that model's full parameter set; the blocks are optional at the schema level, so migrated older files stay valid, and strictly validated when present, because a partially specified sensor is a mistake rather than a smaller sensor.

The structural decisions: rate and latency are configured independently (SENSE-02) and each sensor carries a phase, because sensors do not run on the physics step. The physics runs at 1 kHz and sensors sample on their own schedule, which is what makes motion distortion emerge from the integration rather than being applied to it afterwards (SENSE-01). Latency jitter is the half-width of a uniform distribution, matching what the models implement: transport delay is bounded, and it must not exceed the constant or a message could be stamped before the instant it measured (enforced at build time; JSON Schema cannot compare two fields).

sensors.description: May be empty. A car with no sensors is a legal car for a dynamics-only study, and requiring at least one would make the L0 and L1 tutorials carry a LiDAR they never read.

name.description: Instance name. Becomes the topic name under the agent namespace, so it follows the same character rules as a ROS name.

type.description: Sensor model. lidar_2d, imu and wheel_encoder are built; lidar_3d arrives in P4 (SENSE-06) and is refused by name until then, never substituted by a simpler sensor.

rate.description: Sample rate. [Hz] Independent of the physics rate and of the latency below. For a scanning LiDAR this is the revolution rate, and one scan takes one revolution.

phase.description: Offset of this sensor's first sample within its period, as a fraction. [-] Two sensors at the same rate with different phases do not sample together, which is the normal situation on a real car and a common source of surprise in a simulator that ignores it.

mount.description: Name of the frame in the URDF this sensor is mounted to. The TF tree that runs on the real car owns the transform, so it is referenced here rather than duplicated, and nothing in the simulator consumes it.

latency.description: Transport and processing delay, modelled separately from rate (SENSE-02): a sensor publishing at 40 Hz with 25 ms of delay is not the same as one publishing at 40 Hz without it.

jitter.description: Half-width of the uniform jitter about the constant; must not exceed it, which is enforced at build time. [s]

dropout_probability.description: Per-sample dropout probability, before any material factor the world reports (SENSE-03). Consumed by the LiDAR model. [-]

lidar_2d.description: The 2D scanning LiDAR's parameters. Every ray is individually timestamped and the scan takes one revolution (SENSE-01); the sector is stated in the sensor frame relative to the car's heading.

angle_min.description: Start of the angular sector, sensor frame, positive left (ISO 8855). [rad]

angle_max.description: End of the angular sector; must exceed angle_min, enforced by the model. [rad]

range_min.description: Below this the unit reports nothing. [m]

range_max.description: Beyond this the unit reports nothing. [m]

noise_base.description: Range noise floor: the standard deviation at zero range. [m]

noise_per_metre.description: Range noise growth: standard deviation added per metre of range. [-]

imu.description: The IMU's three error mechanisms on their three timescales: white noise stated as a density (per root hertz, so sampling faster gives noisier samples and the same answer after averaging), a bias random walk that averaging does not remove, and fixed scale errors that are properties of the unit. Initial biases are stated, not drawn: zero is a legitimate and unusual value.

accel_scale_error.description: Fixed multiplicative error; 0.01 reads 1 per cent high. [-]

wheel_encoder.description: Wheel encoders and the odometry built from them. The radius here is deliberately the one somebody typed into a config file, allowed to disagree with the car's own wheel_radius, because typing the wrong one is a common and instructive failure. Needs a tier that computes wheel speeds (L2 and above), which is enforced at build time by name.

counts_per_revolution.description: Counts per full wheel revolution, after gearing and quadrature decoding. [-]

wheel_radius.description: The radius the odometry multiplies by. [m]

wheels_used.description: Which wheels the odometry averages, in the core's wheel order: front-left, front-right, rear-left, rear-right. A rear-drive car with a motor encoder measures the driven wheels and has the worst possible odometry under acceleration, which is the honest default to state.
